title: Speculative Futures on ChatGPT and Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI): A Collective Reflection from the Educational Landscape
extended_summary:
This paper examines the promises and pitfalls of ChatGPT and generative AI in education through a speculative, future-oriented lens rather than an empirical intervention study. The authors aim to surface emerging themes, including potential benefits such as personalized learning, language support, accessibility, faster feedback, and time savings, alongside harms and risks such as bias, privacy concerns, weakened academic integrity, reduced creativity, over-reliance, teacher replacement, and unequal access.

The approach is a collective writing exercise in which a large international group of education scholars wrote fictional narratives imagining positive and negative AI futures. The paper includes multiple speculative stories set across educational contexts, including school-age learners, university students, and educators, but it does not evaluate a real-world deployment of ChatGPT in a controlled study. Instead, it reflects on how AI might reshape learning, teaching, assessment, and academic work.

The main conclusion is that generative AI can support educational tasks but should not be adopted uncritically. The authors argue that education must remain human-centered, that educators should retain the leading role, and that AI use should be ethical, intentional, and context-sensitive. They emphasize the need for AI literacy, new assessment practices, and safeguards around equity, privacy, and bias before large-scale adoption.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI’s conversational generative AI / large language model chatbot used for text generation, question answering, summarization, and other language tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper discusses ChatGPT as the central example of generative AI in education and includes a fictional narrative generated by ChatGPT; it is not an empirical evaluation of a teacher-coaching or lesson-feedback intervention.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a speculative, conceptual paper using fictional narratives and collective reflection rather than a systematic or empirical study design. It does not report measurable outcomes, sample sizes, or effect estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: No causal or quantitative impact on K–12 coaching, lesson feedback, or teacher practice is reported. The paper identifies possible risks and opportunities only at a narrative level.
